rv.q: Thanks to both Purl and Williams, if your heart doesn’t break for Sharon, perhaps you should go see your cardiologist.
And it's one of the best (more-or-less) solo shows I've seen in ages.
Even with those slower passages, Crazy Mama is funny, compassionate, dramatic, and devastating.
The reason to see Crazy Mama isn't the opening-night glamour. It's Linda Purl.

cn.t: Critics praise Linda Purl's extraordinary performance in this moving solo show, with reviewers calling her multi-character work a "thing of beauty" in Sharon Scott Williams' heartrending memoir about growing up with a schizophrenic mother.
